sections.h2: Where is the Rockingham County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is at 170 NC Hwy 65, Suite 150, in Reidsville, NC 27320. The phone is 336-342-8820 and the fax is 336-342-6209. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., although the recording policy page says documents are taken from 8:00 to 4:30, excluding holidays.

The register of deeds is an elected county office, and in Rockingham County it keeps the official land records for deeds, deeds of trust, plats and similar instruments. Staff say plainly that they are a recording agency. They cannot complete forms for you or run a title search, so a seller usually works through a closing attorney who prepares the deed and brings it for recording.

sections.h2: How do I record a deed in Rockingham County?
sections.html:
Present a deed that meets the office's checklist, pay the recording fee and the excise tax, and the office records it in the order described below. The Rockingham County checklist for deeds includes these points:

  • A deed or deed of trust prepared in North Carolina must show the name of the person or law firm that drafted it on the first page.
  • A deed needs the grantee's mailing address on its face, used for tax billing.
  • A document that requires notarization needs a signed acknowledgment with the official's seal and commission expiration date.
  • The excise stamp amount belongs on the face of a conveyance, or the letters NTC (no taxable consideration) if no tax is due.
  • Do not put Social Security, bank, card or driver license numbers in the document unless the law requires it, or only the last four digits.
  • Mailed instruments need a check or money order payable to Rockingham County Register of Deeds and a stamped, self-addressed return envelope. The office charges $25 for a returned check.

Most Rockingham County sellers never touch this list, because the closing attorney handles it. It is still worth knowing if you are deeding property to a family member or into a trust.

sections.h2: What formatting rules apply to documents in Rockingham County?
sections.html:
Documents must follow G.S. 161-14 standards or the office adds a $25 non-standard fee on top of the recording fee. The county lists the standards: letter or legal paper, a 3-inch blank top margin on the first page, quarter-inch margins elsewhere, black type on white paper, a stated instrument type at the top, a font of at least 9 points, and text on one side of the page only.

Blanks and corrections may be made in pen, preferably black. Satisfactions, cancellations and military discharges are exempt, and separate plats follow G.S. 47-30 instead. The register has discretion to waive the fee for a slightly smaller font if the print is legible and reproducible, but the county recommends staying above nine points.

sections.h2: In what order does Rockingham County process documents?
sections.html:
In-person submissions go first, then e-recordings, then priority mail, then regular mail. The county's policy page spells out that order, and it adds that a person who appears at the counter has the document reviewed on the spot and recorded first if it meets the requirements.

The 4:30 p.m. cutoff applies to both paper and electronic filings. A person in line at 4:30 is served that day, while later arrivals are not accepted for recording that day. If the exact recording date matters, deliver the instrument in person and wait to confirm it was recorded before leaving.

Electronic recording is available during business hours. The county lists the benefits as immediate return of the recorded document, no travel and instant feedback if a document is rejected. Ask the office for the current list of approved e-recording vendors.

sections.h2: What does North Carolina charge to record and transfer a deed?
sections.html:
The state sets uniform recording fees, and the grantor pays an excise tax on the sale price. The register collects both before recording, and the numbers below are as printed in the statutes.

State recording fees and excise tax collected by the Rockingham County register
ItemAmount in the statute
Instrument in general$26.00 for the first 15 pages, plus $4.00 for each additional page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for the first 35 pages, plus $4.00 for each additional page
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, plus $2.00 each additional page
Non-standard document add-on$25.00
Satisfaction or cancellationNo fee
Excise tax on conveyance$1.00 on each $500 or fractional part of the consideration

The Rockingham County checklist shows how the rounding works. Under its example, a price of $27,900 is rounded up to $28,000 and the tax is $56. The transferor must pay it before the deed is recorded, so in a typical sale it comes out of the seller's proceeds. Half the tax goes to the county general fund and half to the state.

sections.h2: Why does recording matter when I sell a Rockingham County house?
sections.html:
A conveyance is not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. Priority follows the order and time of registration, which is why a buyer's attorney insists on recording right after funding.

For a seller, the practical points are a clean chain of title, satisfied mortgages and no open liens. Ask the register about a satisfaction that was never recorded, since recording a satisfaction carries no fee. If the title shows a gap, such as an heir who never deeded property after a death, fix it before listing, because it can delay or kill a closing.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Rockingham County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is at 170 NC Hwy 65, Suite 150, Reidsville, NC 27320, and the phone is 336-342-8820. It is open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax on a Rockingham County deed?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor, pays $1.00 per $500 or fractional part of the price to the register before the deed is recorded. Write NTC on the document if no tax is due.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed by mail in Rockingham County?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the original with a check or money order payable to Rockingham County Register of Deeds and a stamped, self-addressed envelope. Never mail cash. Regular mail is recorded after in-person, e-recording and priority mail items.

faqs.q: What time is the recording cutoff?
faqs.a: The cutoff is 4:30 p.m. for both paper and electronic filings. A person in line at 4:30 is served that day, but later arrivals are not accepted for recording that day.

faqs.q: Does the register of deeds give legal advice or run title searches?
faqs.a: No. The office states that it is a recording agency and cannot help complete forms or perform a title search, so ask a closing attorney or title company.
